newRun.title: New inventory run
newRun.hint: Pick a paging scheme and parameters. The run uses the currently initialized scene.
newRun.name: Name (optional)
newRun.adaptiveKHint: Classic DFSA: round 1 uses the Initial $K$; later rounds set $K \approx 2\hat{N}$ from the Schoute / empty-slot backlog estimate. Off: every round uses the same fixed $K$. Only used when the controller below is “auto”; an explicit fixed / DFSA / RL-policy controller overrides it (RL policies come from the Training page).
newRun.useGroupingHint: Periodic paging only. Devices are split into $N_g$ groups; each paging round invites one group in turn. A device joins the group of the first paging it hears (first-catch) and stays aligned to that group's paging times. Off: every paging round invites all devices.
newRun.useCaptureHint: When several devices pick the same Msg1 slot, the reader still decodes the strongest one if it is at least 6 dB above the next strongest. Off: every slot with two or more devices is a collision. For periodic paging the Msg2/Msg3 allocation is $0.5\,K$ with capture and $0.37\,K$ without.
newRun.useEbiHint: EBI is the early indicator (EI) of the aperiodic paper: after Msg1 the reader sends a one-bit flag per slot saying whether a response was detected, so devices know where their Msg2 is. On: each round spends that extra EI air time, and the reader's energy detector is modelled with false alarms and missed detections. Off: no EI time and ideal slot detection.
newRun.includeD2rHint: D2R is the device-to-reader uplink. On: a reader covers a device only if both legs close, so the range is $\min(R2D, D2R)$, as in the paper. Off: only the reader-to-device leg (power-up and paging) counts, which overstates coverage.
newRun.disableReadersHint: Checked readers are skipped for this run (handy for single-reader baselines).
newRun.allReadersDisabledWarning: All readers disabled — no device will be identified.
newRun.endHint: The run ends when every reachable device is identified, when nothing new is identified for the time above, or when you pause / stop it. Devices outside every reader’s coverage are marked unreachable at start; devices never identified are shown as red dots.
newRun.staggerHint: Off: every reader starts its first frame at t = 0. On: readers start in groups, each group a fixed interval after the previous one. The grouping is a strategy and is stored with the run.

controller.title: Frame-size controller
controller.hint: How each reader chooses K and p* every round.
controller.autoFixed: Adaptive K is off → fixed K

desc.auto: Same behaviour as before this option existed: the Adaptive K switch decides between DFSA and fixed K.
desc.fixed: Every round uses the Initial K; p* follows the paging rule.
desc.dfsa: Dynamic framed slotted ALOHA: K = 2N̂ from the backlog estimate of the previous frame.
desc.policy: A trained PPO policy from the registry chooses K and p* from each reader’s local observation. Each reader keeps its own recurrent state.

controller.noPolicies: No policy in the registry yet — train one and promote it (Training page).
controller.deterministicHint: Use the mean action instead of sampling from the policy distribution (reproducible runs).

resource.title: Multi-reader resources
resource.hint: How readers share time and frequency and whether they interfere.

desc.independent: Readers never interfere — the original thesis model and the golden regression.
desc.shared: Every reader uses all F subbands at the same time; overlapping coverage loses R2D/D2R messages.
desc.fdma: The conflict graph is coloured; each colour gets a disjoint group of the F subbands (fewer Msg1 subbands per reader).
desc.tdma: Each colour gets its own time slot in a repeating window; readers wait for their slot (serial within a conflict).
desc.hybrid: Colours are split into frequency groups first, then into time slots inside each group.
desc.lbt: A reader senses the channel before a frame and backs off while a conflicting reader transmits; ETSI dwell rule (max on-time, then a pause).

resource.singleReader: Only one reader is active: coordination has no effect.
resource.fFreqHint: Number of Msg1 frequency subbands (TR 38.769: F). K = L_s × F_r slots per frame.
resource.tdmaWindowHint: Length of one colour’s window in the TDMA superframe (colours × window). Default 0.5 s.
resource.freqGroupsHint: Hybrid: number of disjoint subband groups the colours are spread over; colours sharing a group take turns in time. Default 2.
resource.lbtBackoffHint: Wait after sensing a busy channel.
resource.lbtDwellHint: ETSI EN 302 208 style dwell: after the max on-time the reader must be silent for the pause (default 4 s / 0.1 s).
resource.linkBudgetHint: Two readers conflict if either one’s carrier reaches devices of the other above the SIR limit. Off: a plain distance threshold.
resource.nColorsHint: Empty = greedy colouring decides (minimum it finds).
resource.interferenceHint: Drop messages whose SIR/SINR is below the limits while overlapping readers transmit.
resource.crossMsg1Hint: Msg1 from devices of different readers on the same subband and slot collide.
resource.cwSuppressionHint: How much of another reader’s carrier the receiver cancels (TR 38.769 assumes self-interference cancellation).

termination.title: Reader termination
termination.hint: When a reader decides its population is done — without knowing the ground truth.

desc.oracle: The reader stops when no reachable device is left (simulator knowledge, the old behaviour).
desc.quiet_rounds: Stop after n consecutive frames with no new identification.
desc.id_rate: Stop when the identification rate over a window falls below an absolute or relative threshold.
desc.energy_bound: Stop once every device type has had the worst-case charging time (t_wc) since the last identification, so no sleeping device can still wake up.
desc.combined: Combine several rules with AND (all must fire) or OR (first one wins).

termination.rRelHint: Fraction of the peak rate seen so far.
termination.energySourceHint: Edge: the coverage-edge harvest (conservative). Actual: the reader’s own best-case device.
termination.edgeCapHint: Farthest distance used for the worst case. Device 2b is heard up to ~137 m but cannot harvest beyond ~62 m (ξ = 0 below −41 dBm), so without a cap t_wc is infinite and the rule never fires. 41.4 m = Device 2a coverage, the farthest backscatter device. Untick to use each type's own coverage radius.
termination.maxWaitHint: Upper bound on the wait after the last ID: the reader stops after min(t_wc × (1 + margin), this). Untick for no bound.

charts.termination: Termination rules: extra time vs missed devices

analysis.tNote: Tx = simulated time until x % of all devices in the scene are identified.

retention.hint: G = (T_serial − T_run) / (T_serial − T_ideal) on T99 of the reachable devices. 1 keeps the whole ideal multi-reader gain (independent readers), 0 is no better than serving conflicting readers one after another (TDMA).
retention.needTwo: Select at least two runs (ideal and serial references plus the runs to compare).
retention.unreached: A reference run never reached 99 % of its reachable devices — G is undefined.
retention.degenerate: The serial reference is less than 5 % slower than the ideal one, so readers barely conflict here and G is undefined or blows up. Pick references that differ, or a denser scene.

termination.hint: Each rule is replayed on the recorded frame history of one finished oracle run: how long after the last identification the readers would keep paging (extra time) against how many reachable devices they would leave behind. Bold rows are on the Pareto front.
termination.needFinished: Select at least one finished run.
termination.summary: {{reachable}} reachable · T99 {{t99}} s · last ID {{tLast}} s
termination.notOracle: This run already used a non-oracle rule; the replay only sees frames up to its own stop, so rules that would stop later are cut off.
termination.multiApprox: Several readers: each is replayed on its own frame history. A device its reader would only have found after stopping counts as missed, although in a live run a neighbouring reader might still have found it, so missed devices are an upper bound (see the design doc).
termination.zoomed: The axis is zoomed to the cluster. Rules that keep paging much longer (up to {{max}} s) are the triangles on the right edge.

interference.hint: Messages lost to other readers per run, the time readers waited for their TDMA slot / LBT backoff, and a per-frame timeline of the selected run.
interference.timelineHint: One row per reader; a marker is a frame, its size the number of lost messages.

devices.hint: Distributions over all devices of a finished run (and per device type in the table).

charts.timeBin: Simulated time (s, all readers per bin)

ident.lead: Devices identified so far versus simulated time.
ident.body: X axis is simulated time, Y axis is how many devices some reader has successfully inventoried by then (count or percent). With one reader selected, only devices inside its coverage count. The earlier the curve reaches the top, the faster the inventory. T50 / T90 / T99 are read off this curve. The vertical line is the current live or replay time.

controller.lead: Per round: frame size K, access probability p*, and backlog estimate n̂.
controller.body: Top: K is the number of M1 slots the reader opens in this round (frame length), p* is the probability a device takes part; both are adjusted by the estimator from the previous round. Bottom: n̂ is how many devices the estimator believes are still unidentified, 'true backlog' is the real number, 'joiners' is how many actually took part. n̂ close to the true backlog means the estimator is accurate. With all readers selected only K and the true backlog are drawn, one line per reader.

outcome.lead: How each M1 slot ended, and the share of useful slots.
outcome.body: Each bar is one round (a time bin when all readers are shown), stacked by outcome: success = exactly one device answered, collision = several answered at once and drowned each other, empty = nobody answered. Resource efficiency = success / all slots, on the right axis in percent. Pure slotted ALOHA tops out around 36.8%.

timing.lead: How long each stage of a round took, in milliseconds.
timing.body: A round is paging (reader broadcasts the page) → M1 (devices answer in one of K random slots) → EBI (the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded) → M2 (reader acknowledges each winner) → M3 (device confirms). The stacked height is the whole round. Larger K makes M1 longer; more successes make M2 / M3 longer. With all readers selected the bars are averages per round within each time bin.

energy.lead: Stored energy of the devices now, and protocol energy spent over time.
energy.body: Left: histogram of the energy (µJ) each in-scope device has in its capacitor at the current time; devices on the far left are about to switch off. Right: cumulative energy each device type has spent sending and receiving protocol messages. A device that runs out mid-round is forced off to recharge and competes again later; those events are counted as depletions in Metrics.

round.lead: Slot-by-slot view of one M1 frame.
round.body: Each cell is one M1 slot: idle, single (one device, decoded), captured (several devices, the strongest was decoded), collision, or missed. The numbers above: candidates = awake devices allowed to take part; joiners = those that actually did, after p*; budget = how many winners M2 can acknowledge this round; budget dropped = winners not acknowledged for lack of budget, who retry next round; identified = devices finished in this round; true backlog = devices in this reader's coverage still unidentified. Use the slider to pick a round or follow the latest one.

metrics.lead: Summary numbers and breakdown tables for this run.
metrics.body: Cards: identified / unidentified / resource efficiency / rounds / depletions / unreachable. Per type: count, identified, T50, T99 and energy per device type. Depletions by stage: in which stage devices ran out of energy. Time overhead: total time and share per stage. Per reader: rounds, identified and efficiency for each reader.

pin.lead: Distribution of the strongest power each device receives from any reader.
pin.body: X axis is received power (dBm), Y axis is the fraction of devices receiving at most that power. A curve further right means devices are closer to a reader and harvest faster. One line per device type; compare with Figure 4 of the paper.

coord.lead: How the readers shared the spectrum and what they lost to each other.
coord.body: KPIs: coordination mode, number of colours, frames hit by interference, readers stopped. Bars: messages lost to interference over time per stage (R2D paging, Msg1, Msg2, Msg3). Table: per-reader colour, subbands, time slot, conflict neighbours, rounds, losses, deferred time (TDMA wait / LBT backoff), stop reason and t_wc.

terms.identified: Devices a reader has successfully inventoried.
terms.dropped: Devices still unidentified when the run ended: outside every reader’s coverage, time limit reached, or no progress (shown as red dots).
terms.unreachable: Devices outside every reader's coverage; they can never be inventoried.
terms.no_progress: The run ended by itself after the configured stall time (default 300 s simulated) without a single new identification.
terms.depletions: Times a device ran out of energy in the middle of a round and had to recharge.
terms.rounds: Rounds executed so far, all readers together.
terms.t50: T50 / T90 / T99: simulated time until 50 / 90 / 99 % of the devices were identified.
terms.K: Frame size: number of M1 slots in this round.
terms.pstar: p*: probability that an awake device takes part in this round.
terms.nHat: n̂: the estimator's guess of how many devices are still unidentified.
terms.backlogTrue: True backlog: actual number of unidentified devices in coverage.
terms.joiners: Devices that actually took part in the round after the p* draw.
terms.candidates: Awake devices that were allowed to take part.
terms.success: Slot with exactly one answering device.
terms.collision: Slot where several devices answered at once; none decoded.
terms.efficiency: Resource efficiency: successful slots divided by all slots.
terms.paging: Paging: the reader broadcasts the round parameters.
terms.m1: M1: devices answer in one of K random slots.
terms.ebi: EBI: the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded; its length grows with K.
terms.m2: M2: the reader acknowledges each decoded device.
terms.m3: M3: the acknowledged device replies and is identified.
terms.budget: Maximum number of winners M2 can acknowledge this round.
terms.budgetDropped: Winners not acknowledged because the budget ran out; they retry next round.
terms.energyNow: Energy stored in the device capacitor at the current time.
terms.energySpent: Cumulative energy spent on protocol messages.
terms.slotCodes: Cell colours: idle, single, captured, collision, missed.
terms.pin: Pin: strongest received power from any reader, in dBm.
terms.cdf: CDF: fraction of devices at or below the value on the X axis.
terms.conflictGraph: Conflict graph: an edge joins two readers whose carriers would break each other’s links (link budget or distance).
terms.colour: Colour: a graph colouring of the conflict graph; readers of one colour never conflict and share a resource.
terms.grant: Grant: the subbands and time slot a reader may use.
terms.r2dLost: R2D lost: devices that missed the paging because of another reader’s carrier.
terms.d2rLost: D2R lost: Msg1/Msg3 replies whose SINR at the reader was below the limit.
terms.deferred: Deferred: time a reader waited for its TDMA slot or LBT backoff/pause.
terms.stopReason: Stop reason: which termination rule ended the reader (or exhausted under the oracle).

training.title: Multi-reader RL training
training.subtitle: Experiments under backend/training: learning curves, generalization against DFSA and the policy registry used by runs.
training.noRuns: No run yet. Start one with the command above.
training.learningHint: One dot per training episode; the line is a rolling mean.
training.evalHint: Paired evaluation: the policy and DFSA see the same deployments (readers × device count × mix × offsets). Cell value T99 / DFSA, below 1 (green) means faster than DFSA.
training.promoteHint: Copies the checkpoint into rl/policies with a SHA-256 sidecar so New run can select it.
training.registryHint: Policies that thesis runs can use (controller “RL policy”). ✗ means the file is missing or its hash does not match.

steps_.train: Train offline: cd Implements/backend && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m training.train --config <experiment> --scale small (smoke · small · medium · full, or a factor such as 0.5).
steps_.outputs: Each run writes training/outputs/<experiment>/<stamp>__a…__b…__s…/: meta.json, train_metrics.csv, checkpoints/final.zip + final.json, plots/.
steps_.evaluate: Evaluation runs automatically after training (paired with DFSA); re-run it with python -m training.evaluate --runs <dir> --grid full.
steps_.promote: Promote a good run (button above, --promote, or python -m training.promote <dir>); this copies it into the registry.
steps_.use: In New run pick controller “RL policy” and the policy id; every reader runs the policy with its own state.

training.interruptedHint: The training process ended without finishing (killed or the machine restarted). Start it again with the command above.
